title: Australian Passport Photo Size (mm, cm and Inches)
metaTitle: Australian Passport Photo Size: 35x45 to 40x50mm, Head Size
metaDescription: Australian passport photo size: 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, head 32-36 mm chin to crown. Sizes in mm, cm and inches, and how to measure.
excerpt: The exact Australian passport photo size in millimetres, centimetres and inches, the 32-36 mm head rule, and how it compares with UK and US photos.
keyTakeaways: Photo size: 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high (3.5-4.0 x 4.5-5.0 cm).
Head size: 32-36 mm from chin to crown.
35 x 45 mm is inside the range and is the size most providers print.
A UK or EU template can give a head that is too small for Australia.
intro: **Quick answer:** An Australian passport photo is 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, with the head measuring 32-36 mm from chin to crown. In centimetres that is 3.5-4.0 cm wide x 4.5-5.0 cm high, and in inches about 1.38-1.57 in wide x 1.77-1.97 in high.
**[Check my photo with the Australian passport photo checker →](/australian-passport-photo-checker)**
This page covers size only. For background, pose, glasses and print rules, see the full [Australian passport photo requirements](/guides/australian-passport-photo-requirements).

sections.heading: What size is an Australian passport photo?

subsections.heading: Size in mm, cm and inches
content: How we converted: divide millimetres by 10 for centimetres, and by 25.4 for inches. For example, 35 ÷ 25.4 = 1.378, which rounds to 1.38 inches, and 50 ÷ 25.4 = 1.969, which rounds to 1.97 inches.

subsections.heading: Head height: 32-36 mm
content: The head is measured from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head (the crown). On the print, it must be 32-36 mm.
On a 45 mm high photo, that means your head fills roughly 71-80% of the height. This is a tight, close-up frame.

subsections.heading: Why a range, not one size?
content: The Passport Office allows any width from 35 to 40 mm and any height from 45 to 50 mm.
The head rule does not change with the photo size. It is always 32-36 mm.

subsections.heading: When 35x45mm is the safer choice
content: 35 x 45 mm is at the small end of the range and is a very common passport photo size. Most providers already print it, so it is the easiest size to ask for.
Just make sure the head is 32-36 mm, not the smaller head size used by some other countries.

subsections.heading: When 40x50mm works
content: 40 x 50 mm is at the top of the range and is also allowed. It gives a little more space around the head.
The head must still be 32-36 mm, so a larger photo does not mean a larger head.

subsections.heading: Do not trim a larger photo
content: Do not cut down a bigger photo to fit. Trimming can leave uneven edges and move your head off centre.
Professional providers print to the correct size, so ask for the size you need.

sections.heading: How does the Australian size compare with other countries?

subsections.heading: Australia vs UK
content:
| | Australia | UK |
|---|---|---|
| Photo size | 35-40 x 45-50 mm | 35 x 45 mm |
| Head size | 32-36 mm | 29-34 mm |
The outside size can match, but the UK allows a smaller head. A UK photo with a 29-31 mm head is too small for Australia.

subsections.heading: Australia vs US
content: A US passport photo is 2 x 2 inches (about 51 x 51 mm). It is square, so it is the wrong shape and too wide for an Australian passport.

subsections.heading: Why you cannot reuse a UK or US photo without checking
content: Even if the size looks right, the head height, print method and paper may not meet Australian rules. Australian photos need dye-sublimation prints on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm.
Always check a photo made for another country against the Australian rules first.

sections.heading: How do you check the size of your photo?

subsections.heading: Measure the print with a ruler
content: Use a ruler with millimetre marks. Measure the width across the bottom and the height down one side.
The width should be 35-40 mm and the height 45-50 mm.

subsections.heading: Check the head from chin to crown
content: Place the ruler at the bottom of the chin and measure to the top of the head. The result should be 32-36 mm.
Measure to the top of the head itself, not the top of a hairstyle that sits well above it.

subsections.heading: Check it with our tool
content: Upload a photo to our [Australian passport photo checker](/australian-passport-photo-checker). It estimates the head height and frame and flags problems with the background and lighting.
A pass is a helpful guide, not an approval from the Passport Office.

faq.question: What is the Australian passport photo size in cm?
faq.answer: An Australian passport photo is 3.5-4.0 cm wide x 4.5-5.0 cm high. The head, from chin to crown, must be 3.2-3.6 cm. These come from the official sizes of 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, with a 32-36 mm head, divided by 10 to convert to centimetres.

faq.question: What is the Australian passport photo size in inches?
faq.answer: An Australian passport photo is about 1.38-1.57 inches wide x 1.77-1.97 inches high. The head must be about 1.26-1.42 inches from chin to crown. We converted from millimetres by dividing by 25.4 and rounding to two decimal places. Measure in millimetres if you can.

faq.question: Is the Australian passport photo size the same as 35x45mm?
faq.answer: 35 x 45 mm is allowed, because it sits inside the official range of 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high. It is the size most providers print. The important extra rule is the head size: 32-36 mm from chin to crown, which is larger than some countries allow.

faq.question: What is the head size for an Australian passport photo?
faq.answer: The head must measure 32-36 mm from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head. This rule is the same whatever photo size you choose inside the range. It is the measurement people most often get wrong when they use a template made for another country.

faq.question: Can I use a 2x2 inch photo for an Australian passport?
faq.answer: No. A 2 x 2 inch photo is the US size, about 51 x 51 mm. It is square and wider than the 35-40 mm Australia allows. Do not trim it down either, because that can leave the head the wrong size or off centre. Get photos printed at the Australian size.
